It covers properties from from `Script` types. Script types are more generic than GDScript (`CLASS` types) and can only be supported through the `Script` interface, while for GDScript we can use the internal AST, which allows us more inference. This could be scripts in other script languages like C#, or GDScripts that were obtained from a scene file (since the info that is a GDScript gets lost there).

(Although I added code to upgrade Script types to class Types to some code paths a while ago, since in general the Script type support is more buggy than the CLASS type one.)

According to the [official specification](https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/lsp/3.17/specification/#completionItem), it sounds like `CompletionItem.deprecated` is itself deprecated:
```typescript
export interface CompletionItem {
	...
	/**
	 * Indicates if this item is deprecated.
	 *
	 * @deprecated Use `tags` instead if supported.
	 */
	deprecated?: boolean;
	...
}
```
I thought I checked and found that VS Code, at least, didn't support `CompletionItem.deprecated`, but I can take another look. 

It looks like we may also be able to check the client's capabilities via [`CompletionClientCapabilities`](https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/lsp/3.17/specification/#completionClientCapabilities), including whether or not they support either `CompletionItem.deprecated` or `CompletionItemTag.Deprecated`.

I know, that's how it's supposed to work. But our server implementation doesn't implement capability tracking. We just ignore the capabilities that a client sends. I was hoping `deprecated` would work even if it is deprecated in the protocol. When we add tags without proper capability tracking we risk breaking other client implementations that aren't up to date.

I originally didn't want to implement capability tracking before limiting clients to 1 client per server (see https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/11056). But if this becomes a blocker it should be possible to just save them per client for now (at the risk of breaking some assumptions when multiple clients are connected).

I think you shouldn't use `get_global_name()` to determine the doc class name. Because for unnamed classes, inner classes and autoload singletons the name may differ from the global name.

After #91060 there is a new method `Script::get_doc_class_name()`, but there is no counterpart for `GDScriptParser::ClassNode`. I reused `GDScriptDocGen::doctype_from_gdtype()` (which uses `GDScriptDocGen::_get_class_name()`).

This is preloaded type. There are two deprecation flags that could be attached to it. The class/script to which the variable points is deprecated or the constant which holds the script is deprecated. This currently only seems to handle the later case, but the first case is far more important in this case.
If this constant holds a script (`is_meta_type`) the deprecation status of this script should be taken into account as well.

As I recall, `class_doc_map` just has the class names themselves, not the enum names. `type` from above is defined as `base_type.native_type.get_slicec('.', 0)` so that if statement is just checking if the first component of the type string (the class name) is in `class_doc_map`.
